text:
maya: Heads up — multiple hosted inference customers are reporting sudden 502/504 spikes out of us-west2 during the last ~10m. Support has an escalated ticket. Anyone seeing infra alerts?

raj: seeing it in the gateway metrics — 5xx rate up ~6x from baseline, error signature looks like upstream read timeouts. Affected edge: wc-us-west2-a and wc-us-west2-b.

derek: checking network graphs now. I can see packet-loss increase between our edge POPs and the transit provider for that region, loss ~2-5% persisting, RTT jump ~80ms.

lina: customer repro steps from support: run a request loop to hosted API -> ~30% of requests fail with 502, usually after ~3-5s. They included curl output: 
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\nx-server-error: upstream_read_timeout\n"\n

raj: grabbing `mtr` from one of the affected edge hosts, output: 
```
Start: host-edge-12
 1. 10.0.0.1                   0.2%  0.2ms
 2. transit-pe-1.example.net    0.0%  1.1ms
 3. transit-core.example.net    3.6%  12.4ms  ### loss starts here
 4. provider-as64512-gw         3.6%  13.1ms
 5. provider-agg                3.6%  95.2ms
```

maya: that bridge at hop 3/4 aligns with where the carrier is showing microbursts. Is that the same ASN we use for us-west2?

net-eng-bot: AS path lookup for provider IP shows origin ASN 64512, peering at SFO-IX. No active BGP flaps in our routers.

derek: BGP looks stable on our side, but provider-side telemetry shows intermittent queueing leading to packet drops. They've acknowledged higher queue depth on a peering interface.

support-ops: impacted customers: acme-payments (P1), psi-media (P2). Both report degraded throughput and increased API retries. Acme is threatening to failover to a competitor if this persists.

lina: quick mitigation options: 1) enable region-fallback policy to prefer us-west1 (different provider path) for affected customers, 2) increase gateway retry budget temporarily, 3) route around via our secondary transit if capacity allows. Thoughts?

raj: I can flip fallback for the P1 customers now (low risk). Also rolling a config to increase upstream timeout from 5s -> 8s for the gateway for hosted inference to reduce spurious 502s.

maya: please coordinate with oncall SRE before changing timeouts. We need to avoid masking real backend failures. @oncall-sre can you approve a temporary timeout bump + region-fallback for acme-payments?

oncall-sre: approve for acme-payments only. I'll monitor error budget and latency. Set a 30m window then review.

derek: opened carrier ticket (TICKET-2026-998) and sent traceroute/mtr logs. They say they're seeing a microburst pattern on a PE and are investigating QoS.

net-eng-bot: Created status page incident INC-3852468 and posted initial message to customers (we flagged partial degradation in us-west2).

support-ops: sent acme-payments the workaround steps (enable our region-fallback) and offered temporary Dedicated capacity if they want full isolation. They accepted fallback.

lina: adding simple repro for SRE/Net team to validate: 
1) curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" --data '{"prompt":"test"}' -o /dev/null -s -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" - run for ~100 reqs
2) run `mtr -rwzbc 100 provider-gw-ip` from edge host

raj: after enabling fallback for acme, their error rate dropped from 28% -> 2% within 3m. Good sign.

maya: action items:
- derek: keep carrier ticket open and push for root cause + eta (TICKET-2026-998)
- raj: monitor gateway error budget, revert timeout bump after 30m window
- oncall-sre: monitor SLIs + confirm no backend regressions
- support-ops: keep customer comms and update acme/psi every 15m

derek: provider updated: they identified an overloaded PE queue due to a mis-scheduled maintenance job; they've applied a temporary filter and are rerouting some traffic. ETA to stable: ~45m.

support-ops: acme confirmed reduced errors and will keep their fallback on for 1 hour then test.

maya: good. I'll keep this thread pinned. If carrier doesn't confirm fix in 45m escalate to partnerships and legal (for SLA).

raj: last call — gateway 5xx rate is trending down in metrics, latency still slightly elevated but within SLO.

oncall-sre: marking for post-incident review. Please paste all logs and the carrier ticket summary when available.

maya: thanks team.
